expected_status.description: value of --expect-status; process exit code is 0 iff status == expected_status

command.description: argv of the binary; with --dump-state the relative `--dump-state=state` is appended (relative because cwd is the work dir, so the recorded command carries no host path)

not_applicable.description: true when the case dir has no observables.toml (derived probe cases); MISSING_OUTPUT is then never assigned

core_dump.description: a file named core or core.* appeared in the work dir; status is at least CRASHED

diagnostics.description: every well-formed stderr line starting with `HSTAR_DIAG ` (M1-02 exit protocol: shlex-parsable, schema=1, code, integer exit), parsed as key=value; all records kept, order preserved

value.description: M1-03: offending value (RANGE/REF/DUPLICATE/UNSUPPORTED); empty string when not applicable

allowed.description: M1-03: allowed range or set, e.g. "1..289" or "<=cap"; empty string when not applicable

diagnostics_malformed.description: HSTAR_DIAG lines that failed strict parsing (unbalanced quotes, schema != 1, missing code, non-integer exit/seq/index/iostat/schema), each followed by the reason; non-empty forces status FAILED

check_summary.description: stdout HSTAR_CHECK / HSTAR_CHECK_READER lines (--check-legacy); null when none were emitted. CHECKED requires check_malformed empty, status OK and errors 0

check_malformed.description: deviations of the HSTAR_CHECK* lines from the check-mode contract (unbalanced quotes, missing/duplicate HSTAR_CHECK, schema != 1, mode != check-legacy, non-integer errors/readers_executed/n, readers_executed != number of HSTAR_CHECK_READER lines, zero included); non-empty forces status FAILED

protocol_violation.description: why the status is FAILED (malformed HSTAR_DIAG, exit= outside 2..6, rc != exit=, rc != 0 without diagnostic, unexpected stderr, malformed HSTAR_CHECK, check status != OK or errors != 0 with rc 0, or a requested state dump that does not normalize); null otherwise

state.description: M2-02 state dump (tools/yl_state.py); null unless --dump-state was given. --dump-state is mutually exclusive with --check-legacy (refused by the runner, exit 3). A dump that does not normalize turns CHECKED / MISSING_OUTPUT / COMPLETED into FAILED with protocol_violation `state dump malformed: ...`

dump_dir.description: <work>/state, where the binary wrote one state.txt per checkpoint directory

normalized_dir.description: <run_dir>/state, the canonical tree; null when normalization failed, since nothing is then written

map.description: the field map the dump was validated against

checkpoints.description: per checkpoint id (model_ready, phase_ready(1), increment_ready(1,1)); a checkpoint whose state.txt is missing is absent here and reported in normalize.problems

raw_file.description: path of the raw dump relative to dump_dir, e.g. phase_ready_1/state.txt

fields.description: normalized field entries of that checkpoint, reconstructed ones included

fingerprint.description: sha256 over the sorted per-file digests of the canonical tree; null when normalization failed. Repeat runs of the same case must agree

status.description: classification order (first match wins). INPUT_ERROR/UNSUPPORTED/INIT_ERROR/SOLVE_ERROR/INTERNAL_ERROR: rc 2/3/4/5/6 equal to the exit= of a well-formed HSTAR_DIAG line; FAILED also covers protocol violations (malformed HSTAR_DIAG, exit= outside 2..6, rc != exit=) and a check summary that is malformed or not status=OK/errors=0, and a requested state dump that does not normalize (which demotes CHECKED / MISSING_OUTPUT / COMPLETED only); GOLDEN_MODIFIED outranks CHECKED and COMPLETED
